sections.h2: Where Henry County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
Henry County deeds are filed in Napoleon, in Suite 202 up the stairs in the courthouse at 660 N. Perry Street. The Recorder's number is 419-592-1766, and the counter closes at 4:30 on weekdays, with the doors shut on weekends and holidays.

One recorder covers all of Henry County, roughly 416 square miles. A farm along the Putnam County line and a house inside Napoleon are handled at the same window. The county's recorder page describes the office as the keeper of real estate records and lists what it takes: deeds, mortgages, mechanic's liens, powers of attorney, IRS liens, subdivision plats, military discharges, partnership papers, and the zoning resolutions of the county and its townships.

sections.h2: Why old chains of title matter here
sections.html: Henry County was organized in 1834, so deeds here stretch back through two centuries of farm and town sales. A house that came through an estate or a long-held farm may carry decades of recorded easements, mortgages and affidavits, and the recorder's index is where a title company finds them. Napoleon is both the seat of government and the biggest city.

The Henry County Auditor keeps an office in the same courthouse and answers at 419-592-1956. The auditor's forms page lists the Ohio sale paperwork:

  • DTE 100, the value statement and receipt that goes with a conveyance.
  • DTE 100EX, where you write down why a transfer owes no such fee.
  • DTE 101 for a homestead parcel, DTE 102 for a parcel in the farm valuation program.
  • The Henry County Land Transfer Policy. Ask the auditor's staff for a copy early.

The auditor sees the deed first. Under section 319.202 the buyer files a value statement, the auditor endorses the deed, and a rental house triggers an extra landlord filing under Chapter 5323. Only then does it travel on to the Recorder.

sections.h2: What the Auditor charges on a sale
sections.html:
The auditor's charge comes from section 319.54(G)(3): $1 at minimum, or a dime for each hundred dollars of value if that is more, with part of a hundred counted whole. The seller pays. Get the dollar figure for your price from the counter before closing day.

Any Ohio county may add a transfer tax of up to thirty cents per $100 under section 322.02. The grantor pays it before the Recorder sees the deed. Ask the auditor whether Henry County charges it, and see that your closing statement shows the answer.

Several transfers owe no statement fee, among them a deed for no money, a conveyance worth $100 or less, a deed given only as security, and a division among the heirs of one decedent. DTE 100EX is where the reason goes.

Fees follow section 317.32. Each charge pairs a base fee with a housing trust fund fee of equal size: $17 each for the first two pages and $4 each for every page after. A county may tack on a preservation surcharge of up to $5. Ask the office for the bottom line on your deed.

Pages are counted at 8.5 by 14 inches, and the caption page is page one. A deed that spills a few lines onto a third sheet costs more, so have it formatted tightly.

The state's layout rule in section 317.114 applies too, and some Ohio counties charge $20 for a deed that breaks it. Ask what Henry County adds before you sign one with odd margins or tiny type.

Owners occupy about 82.5% of the occupied homes, and the typical owner-occupied house is valued at $168,600. Only 19 building permits were issued in 2025, so a resale rarely competes with new construction.

About a third of residents lived in urban areas at the 2020 census and two thirds in rural ones, which is why farm parcels and big lots show up in the recorder's queue as often as town lots.

Sheriff sales for orders received after August 1, 2022 run online through RealAuction, and tax sales are held on the first floor of the courthouse. Bidders deposit by wire or ACH, never cash, and deposits are set by appraised value:

  • $2,000 for an appraisal up to $10,000.
  • $5,000 for an appraisal from $10,000 to $200,000.
  • $10,000 for an appraisal above $200,000.

After the auction the buyer waits 30 to 45 days for the court's confirmation and the sheriff's deed. The former owner keeps title until the judge signs, and the new owner gets title only when the sheriff's deed lands in the Henry County Recorder's index. The judgment creditor and the first lienholder can redeem within 14 days by paying the full price to the clerk of courts.

sections.h2: Property tax help in Henry County
sections.html:
The Treasurer sits in the same courthouse, at P.O. Box 546, Napoleon, phone 419-592-1851. Monthly payment plans for unpaid back taxes and current taxes halt added interest and penalties. A Tax Installment Prepay plan splits the yearly bill into coupons with no penalty for a late one, provided each half is paid in full by its closing date.

The county has 40 taxing districts, each with its own rate, and values property at 35% of market. The auditor reappraises every six years and updates in the third. Owners can contest a valuation from January 1 through March 31 before the county Board of Revision, and the 2 1/2% owner-occupancy rollback takes a single application before the first Monday in June.

On the homestead page, the TY2025 figures are a $40,000 income limit and a $28,000 exemption, with more for disabled military service members. Owners who are struggling can contact NOCAC, the Northwestern Ohio Community Action Commission, or Maumee Valley Planning's housing program.

sections.h2: Selling with a mortgage or taxes owed
sections.html: If you still owe on the house, the title company pays off the lender and any unpaid tax from your proceeds at closing, and the lender then records a release. Ask the Treasurer for a payoff figure before the closing date, and ask the auditor whether the parcel carries a homestead reduction, since DTE 101 then goes with the deed. When you hand over the paperwork, bring the parcel number and the legal description from your own deed. Staff can then match the new deed to the tax record quickly, and the Recorder will index it under the right parcel without a callback to the closing agent.

faqs.q: Who records Henry County deeds, and where?
faqs.a: The Henry County Recorder, in Suite 202 on the second floor of the courthouse at 660 N. Perry Street in Napoleon. The phone is 419-592-1766.

faqs.q: Do I visit the auditor before the recorder?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer files a statement of value with the auditor, who endorses the deed. The recorder files it after that. Both offices share the courthouse in Napoleon.

faqs.q: How is the Ohio conveyance fee figured?
faqs.a: It is the larger of $1 or ten cents per $100 of value, with any fraction of $100 counted as a full $100. The seller pays it, subject to the statute's exemptions.

faqs.q: Is there a county transfer tax in Henry County?
faqs.a: Call the auditor to find out. State law lets a county charge up to thirty cents per $100 after two hearings.

faqs.q: Can a sheriff-sale buyer record immediately?
faqs.a: No. The judge must confirm the sale and the sheriff must receive the deed, which takes 30 to 45 days after the auction. Title passes when the sheriff's deed is recorded.
